name: Buku-Larrnggay Mulka Centre
funding: Small community art centre; core IVAIS support since 1998-99, plus NT Government, Ian Potter Foundation and Cotton On Foundation (retail).
watch: Yolŋu community-controlled art centre, founded 1976. A local landowner corporation that earns bauxite royalties gave money in 2017.
records_note: ACNC holds annual reports for 2017 and 2018 and financial reports for 2013 to 2025; the centre's own site lists no funders or board.

name: Casco Art Institute: Working for the Commons
funding: Structural support from Mondriaan Fund, City of Utrecht and Stichting DOEN via Arts Collaboratory.
watch: Moved from an exhibition showroom to a commons-based, cooperative model. Under Binna Choi it rebuilt its governance around feminist economics, mutual care and collective unlearning.
records_note: Its Foundation page says annual and financial reports sit in a public Dropbox folder; the About page names three funders, the Team page the board.

name: Castello di Rivoli Museo d Arte Contemporanea
funding: €6.5M. Regione Piemonte, Città di Torino, Fondazione CRT, Compagnia di San Paolo.

name: Centre d'Art Contemporain Genève
funding: City of Geneva (Ville de Genève), Republic and Canton of Geneva, Swiss Federal Office of Culture (OFC), Loterie Romande. Audited public accounts.

name: Centro Cultural de la República El Cabildo
funding: Cultural arm of Paraguay's National Congress, paid from the congressional budget (a G. 1.88 billion extension for a new building in 2025). Entry to the ground-floor rooms is free.
watch: Shows mid-20th-century to present Paraguayan art, including Olga Blinder and Livio Abramo. A December 2020 fire hit the newer block; the heritage building was safe.
records_note: Its site has programme and news pages only; no reports, accounts, funders or board are posted, and its parent is the Paraguayan Congress.

name: Christchurch Art Gallery
funding: Christchurch City Council; the Christchurch Art Gallery Foundation raises acquisition funds. Partners are JBWere (foundation partner) and Anthony Harper (major partner), plus hotel, design and drinks suppliers.
watch: Public civic art museum in Te Wai Pounamu.
records_note: A council unit with no reports or accounts of its own; partner logos only, no board. Its Foundation files returns on the NZ register.

name: Circle Art Gallery
funding: Limited company owned by art collectors including Samit Gehlot (Intex Foundation), Tony Wainaina and Robert Devereux. It sells at international fairs and runs an annual East African art auction.
watch: Founded in 2012 under director Danda Jaroljmek. Opened its first dedicated gallery in 2015 and joined Cromwell Place, London, in 2020.
records_note: The gallery's site posts no reports, accounts, funder list or board; its About page only names the art collectors who own shares.

name: Contemporary Art Gallery (CAG)
funding: Canada Council, BC Arts Council, BC Gaming Policy and Enforcement Branch, City of Vancouver and Connor, Clark and Lunn Investment Management.
watch: The BC gaming grant is public gambling-proceeds money, which the map grades as an ordinary public funder.
records_note: Lists its board and shows a few undated funder logos; links no annual reports, financial statements or named donor list.

name: Contemporary Art Museum of the Kasbah
funding: Run by the National Foundation of Museums. Restoration and design cost 13 million dirhams; the Wilaya of Tangier supervised it, with the Ministry of Culture, APDN and the Foundation contributing.
watch: Opened in December 2021 in the former Kasbah prison to mark the Foundation's tenth anniversary. Opening show: The School of the North.
records_note: Publishes nothing itself; its operator, the National Foundation of Museums, posts laws and an org chart image but no reports, accounts, donors or board names.

name: Contemporary Arts Museum Houston
funding: Warhol, Teiger, N2 Stone and Frank Liu Jr. foundations, NEA, City of Houston, Texas Commission on the Arts and Major Exhibition Fund donors, per 2026 credits. FY2025 expenses $6.1M.
watch: Non-collecting museum offering free admission to the public.
records_note: No annual reports found; Form 990s for 2011 to 2023 are on ProPublica, no standing donor list exists, and 20 trustees are named.

name: Contemporary Calgary
funding: Individual Leadership Circle and lifetime donors. LOOK gala presented by Mawer (2025), Rogers (2023) and National Bank (2020 to 2022); Holt Renfrew sponsors the dinner.
watch: Housed in the historic Centennial Planetarium.
records_note: Posts a 2024-25 annual report, names its Leadership Circle donors undated and lists sixteen board members; accounts were not checked.

name: Cranbrook Art Museum
funding: Exhibition credits name MillerKnoll, Gilbert Family Foundation, DeRoy Testamentary Foundation and Clannad Foundation. The Gilberts pledged $30M in 2021 to Cranbrook Academy of Art, which also backs museum projects.
watch: National Historic Landmark in Bloomfield Hills, Michigan.
records_note: No records of its own; parent Cranbrook Educational Community posts Form 990s 2020 to 2025 and its trustees, and the museum lists no donors.
